meta.scene_summary: We're busy building the future with AI while the foundation is being held together by duct tape and prayers.

cooking.headline: Cloudflare just adopted the kid who grew up to be better than Node.js
cooking.summary: Cloudflare acquired Deno, essentially bringing the 'I told you so' runtime under the same roof as their edge infrastructure. It turns out the best way to win the JavaScript wars is to just buy the competition until everyone is on your platform.
cooking.plain_english: Cloudflare has purchased the company behind the Deno programming environment to integrate its technology into their global network services.

cooking.headline: TypeSafe raises $870M, proving 'AI' is still the best fundraising keyword
cooking.summary: TypeSafe just raised enough money to buy a small country, confirming that investors are still throwing billions at anything with a generative suffix. At this point, I'm pretty sure you could get a seed round just by naming your startup 'PromptEngineering.ai' and promising to fix the internet.
cooking.plain_english: The artificial intelligence company TypeSafe has raised $870 million in new funding, bringing its total valuation to $7.5 billion.

cooking.headline: Oxide just raised $445M to prove hardware is actually hard
cooking.summary: Oxide Computer is raking in massive funding to build custom servers for people who hate the cloud. It turns out that if you tell VCs you're going to fix the supply chain, they'll happily pay for your custom silicon habit.
cooking.plain_english: Oxide Computer has raised $445 million in funding to develop and sell custom server hardware.

cooking.headline: Science is getting a $1.8B software update to make biology readable by AI
cooking.summary: Scientists are finally standardizing biological data so AI can actually make sense of it instead of treating it like a messy codebase with no documentation. It's a massive investment to turn biology into a queryable database, which is great until the AI decides the most efficient way to solve a disease is to delete the patient.
cooking.plain_english: A global initiative has committed $1.8 billion to organize biological data into a standardized format that is easily accessible and usable by artificial intelligence models.

cooked.headline: OpenAI fires the people whose literal job was to stop them from being evil
cooked.summary: OpenAI let go of three safety researchers, proving that nothing disrupts workplace culture quite like pointing out the fire while the building is still being built. It's the ultimate group project move to fire the person who keeps reminding you that the code doesn't actually work yet.
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI has terminated three employees from its safety research team, citing the improper handling of confidential information.

cooked.headline: OpenAI's head of safety finds out that 'safety' is just a suggestion
cooked.summary: Tomek Korbak was told he is no longer trusted by the company he was hired to keep safe. It turns out the only thing more dangerous than unaligned AI is being the person in the room pointing out that the AI might be unaligned.
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI has removed its head of safety from his role due to a breakdown in internal trust.

cooked.headline: Yandex data centers are having a really bad week
cooked.summary: Yandex just lost two data centers in 48 hours, proving that physical infrastructure is the ultimate single point of failure. It's the digital equivalent of trying to host a website on a laptop that someone keeps throwing out a window.
cooked.plain_english: Yandex experienced significant damage to two of its data centers within a 48-hour period.

cooked.headline: The internet is now just a group project where everyone is using ChatGPT to ghostwrite their contributions.
cooked.summary: An Iranian influence campaign successfully planted AI-generated articles in legitimate US publications. It turns out the biggest threat to journalism isn't the death of truth, but the fact that we're all just reading auto-completed fan fiction now.
cooked.plain_english: An Iranian group used artificial intelligence to create and publish fake news articles in American media outlets.

cooked.headline: Public key cryptography is having a 'this is fine' moment.
cooked.summary: Experts are warning that the foundation of internet security might be on the verge of collapse due to advancements in computing power. It is the digital equivalent of realizing your front door lock is made of wet cardboard right as the neighborhood burglar starts a hobby in lock-picking.
cooked.plain_english: Security experts are concerned that future computing technology may render current methods for protecting digital data and communications ineffective.

cooked.headline: Crypto is preparing for a bunker mode because AI is about to brute-force our private keys
cooked.summary: We spent a decade building decentralized finance only to realize our security model is essentially a math homework assignment that AI is about to ace. It turns out the only thing standing between your wallet and a total wipeout is a quantum-resistant upgrade that we definitely should have started yesterday.
cooked.plain_english: Vitalik Buterin and other experts are concerned that future AI advancements could break existing digital currency security, prompting a push for more robust, future-proof encryption methods.
